hook: SCP-582 is a Keter entity that exists because people write stories about it: any piece of fiction featuring it becomes a real event, carried out the way it was written. It's a short, conceptual file, and much of its pull comes from what the Foundation chooses to black out. Read the list of manifestations closely, since the entries grow stranger and more clipped toward the end.
whyItMatters: The idea folds back on the Foundation itself, because containing something made of stories means controlling stories, down to monitoring search engines and erasing sources. It ties that premise to a small pulp-horror origin: an obscure writer, criticized for imitating Lovecraft, whose unpublished work spread through his friends after his death. The result is a compact meme-hazard article whose threat is narrative rather than physical.
thingsToNotice: Containment is itself a narrative: Manifestation Delta stays put only because its containment story says it cannot leave its chamber or touch staff, and Addendum 3 shows a fragment of that story. Later entries hint at things going wrong, with an Epsilon form declared no longer canon after an event, and a Zeta Prime account cut off mid-story that now triggers an XK scenario protocol. The origin is recursive as well, since the author apparently wrote about his own encounter with the entity decades before writing the stories that started it. The closing note insists it has no will of its own and only ever does what someone wrote.
